newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares may gain on fresh U.S. highs.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares may gain on fresh U.S. highs.

text.p: Singapore shares were expected to start the week a little firmer on Monday, taking heart from a new record high on Wall Street on Friday and from some positive economic news at home.
"I think it could tick up a little, given the strength in the U.S.," said one institutional broker.
The Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) ended down 6.35 points at 2,055.36 on Friday. Malaysian issues drew retail interest with the UOB OTC index gaining 9.23 points to 1,168.06.
New York's Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 87.78 points to close at 7,345.91 on Friday, a fresh record high. For the week it closed up 151.24.
Singapore-based dealers cited better economic statistics as a reason for cautious optimism that the recent downtrend in the local stock market may have ended.
Last week saw the publication of the first positive export figures for Singapore in five months.
Technical analysts hedged their bets with some forecasting a drift lower towards 2,040 before a rally.
